title: Letter 18 — Forsaken by Men, Near to God
attribution_note: Letter 18 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: *“Dear friend and brother in Christ!”*

It is written: *“And my neighbours stood afar off from me”* [Psalm 37:13]. For white and black do not agree; darkness is not at one with light. And between piety and ungodliness there is unceasing warfare. What concord can there be, when one strives toward the mountain and forces himself to climb, and the other rolls downhill?

So then, *“neighbours stood afar off”* from you, because you stood far from them; and you stood far because you found in them nothing kindred to yourself. From soot and tar we withdraw, that we be not blackened; contagious disease we flee, that we be not infected; and from lepers we turn aside, that we ourselves suffer not the same. Therefore it is said: *“Come out from among them, and touch not the unclean thing”* [Isaiah 52:11; 2 Corinthians 6:17; Revelation 18:4].

Whoever withdraws from such as these draws near to God; and the nearer he draws, the more men withdraw from him; and the more men withdraw from him, the more God draws near to him, as to one forsaken by men. *“The poor is left unto Thee; be Thou the helper of the fatherless,”* O Lord my God [Psalm 9:35]! He must be poor whom men forsake.

O God, in whom is all! Let all forsake me, every one of them — only do not You forsake me! In You I shall have all: You are my help, my defence, my strength, my covering, my refuge, my counsel and my consolation.
Therefore, forsaken by men, flee to God, as you ought and as you write. For He finds place to work His work there where the works of men are not. And this is the first.

Second: we must grieve when we offend God; this wound is healed by such a plaster. The offence of God (O God! Who are we? Worms, earth, dust and ashes — we offend Your majesty! Suffer us not to come to this again, by Your grace!), the offence of God, I say, is healed by sorrow according to God. Sin begets sorrow, and by this sorrow it is cured. A bitter offspring is sorrow, yet it destroys its fierce parent — sin. Such is the wondrous wisdom of God: a wound is healed by a wound! *“For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of,”* says the apostle [2 Corinthians 7:10].

*“Thy mercy,”* O God, go before us *“all the days of our life”* [Psalm 22:6]! Save, O Christ God, those whom You came to save, and for whom You shed Your Blood! With this I conclude, committing myself to the mercy of God, and remain...
